[#hash-measurements]
== Measured size and throughput

What each backend costs a program on each target, in bytes and in time, as webcpp measured it
(spec section 4.2). The size of a backend is what matters on WebAssembly, where every byte is
downloaded; its throughput is what matters natively. `detail/ranking.hpp`, generated from the
same data, orders the backends of each key derivation by both, and the default backend follows it.

Measured on 2026-11-15 on Apple M5 Max, 18 cores, 128 GiB, Darwin 27.0.0;
WebAssembly under wasmtime 47.0.3 (5554cc1a6 2026-07-31) (wasip2, wasip3) and node v26.13.0 (Emscripten).
Compilers: native: Apple LLVM 21.0.0 (clang-2100.4.1.1); wasip2: Clang 23.1.0-wasi-sdk (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project 895aa2c896ada719451be2e3673c83da8ddf1141); wasip3: Clang 23.1.0-wasi-sdk (https://github.com/llvm/llvm-project 895aa2c896ada719451be2e3673c83da8ddf1141); emscripten: Clang 24.0.0git (https:/github.com/llvm/llvm-project f718ebe873411a562ef6e5c27da36d75b7aaec98).

WARNING: the machine was shared and loaded while this was measured (many builds ran at once;
1, 5 and 15 minute load averages 40/85/148 before and 64/83/141 after, on 18 cores).
Every time is a median with its spread; read the spread, not a single figure. Sizes do not
depend on the load.

Sizes: the bytes of the program built at variant=release optimization=space: natively the executable stripped with strip, on WebAssembly the .wasm file. Throughput: the program built at variant=release optimization=speed, run with --time: one computation to warm up, then five timed runs of the workload, each repeated `repetitions` times; per invocation the median of its five runs, per record the median of its invocations' medians, with the fastest and slowest run. Orders: by size, a backend moves before the one ahead of it only when its program is smaller; by throughput, only when its median is more than 10 percent below the other's and its slowest run is faster than the other's fastest; otherwise the committed order stands (on a first measurement, the capability table's order of backends). A WebAssembly target orders by its own throughput where every backend of the row ran within the bound, else by the native order.

=== Throughput

A hash or MAC in MiB per second over 1 MiB, a key derivation in time per derivation; the median, then
the slowest and fastest runs. Per function, the workload:

* md5_128: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha1_160: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha2_224: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha2_256: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha2_384: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha2_512: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha2_512_224: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha2_512_256: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha3_224: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha3_256: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha3_384: the hash of 1 MiB.
* sha3_512: the hash of 1 MiB.
* shake_128: the hash of 1 MiB.
* shake_256: the hash of 1 MiB.
* keccak_256: the hash of 1 MiB.
* blake2b_512: the hash of 1 MiB.
* blake2s_256: the hash of 1 MiB.
* blake3: the hash of 1 MiB.
* ripemd_128: the hash of 1 MiB.
* ripemd_160: the hash of 1 MiB.
* siphash_32: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* siphash_64: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_md5_128: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha1_160: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha2_224: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha2_256: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha2_384: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha2_512: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha2_512_224: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha2_512_256: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha3_224: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha3_256: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha3_384: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_sha3_512: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_ripemd_128: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_ripemd_160: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_blake2b_512: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* hmac_blake2s_256: the MAC of 1 MiB under a 32-byte key.
* fnv1a_32: the hash of 1 MiB.
* fnv1a_64: the hash of 1 MiB.
* xxhash_32: the hash of 1 MiB.
* xxhash_64: the hash of 1 MiB.
* xxh3_128: the hash of 1 MiB.
* murmur3_32: the hash of 1 MiB.
* murmur3_128: the hash of 1 MiB.
* spooky2_128: the hash of 1 MiB.
* hkdf_extract: HKDF-Extract of a 32-byte IKM with a 32-byte salt, repeated 1,000 times.
* hkdf_expand: HKDF-Expand of 32 bytes from a digest-size PRK and a 16-byte info, repeated 1,000 times.
* hkdf: HKDF of 32 bytes from a 32-byte IKM, a 32-byte salt and a 16-byte info, repeated 1,000 times.
* pbkdf2: PBKDF2 of 32 bytes from a 16-byte password and salt at 100,000 iterations.
* argon2id: Argon2id of 32 bytes from a 16-byte password and salt at libsodium's interactive costs (2 passes over 64 MiB).
* scrypt: scrypt of 32 bytes from a 16-byte password and salt at N=16384, r=8, p=1 (16 MiB).
